clue.text: Most unlikely pleasure centre provided (2,2)

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: the two middle letters of pleASure
if = provided (that)

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of finding the brain's pleasure centre.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pleasure centre" reads as the brain's reward circuit, but here it only means the middle of the word pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: "As if!" is the scornful reply to something most unlikely.

clue.text: Test shows: "Rather boring, endless diarrhoea" (3,3)

explanation.walkthrough: "The runs" is slang for diarrhoea; drop the S and it becomes RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a rehearsal or trial, which is a test.

clue.text: Ex-PM, playing lyre, gets the wind (9)

explanation.surface: A former prime minister strums a lyre and suffers flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: "Gets the wind" sounds like digestive trouble; the wind is a northerly. Lord North was the Prime Minister who lost the American colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Winds are named for where they blow from, so a northerly is one arriving out of the north.

clue.text: Eye after this seductive look (4)

explanation.definitionFit: The clue defines the word by the idiom it completes: glad plus eye makes a seductive look.

clue.text: & 20ac.What many an oldie will lose with Bury on fire: settlement (6,4)

definitions.text: What many an oldie will lose

blocks.note: cross-reference: the answer continues in 20 across
w = with, as in w/
to inter is to bury
fuel is what goes on a fire

explanation.surface: Pensioners face losses as the Lancashire town of Bury goes up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: The Winter Fuel Payment is a UK benefit for pensioners to help with heating, which the 2024 government withdrew from most of them. Bury looks like the town but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: When the payment was means-tested in 2024, most older people lost it.
